nodes.content: Infer directed cell–cell signaling from spatial transcriptomics while distinguishing shared microenvironment effects under incomplete molecular observation.
requirements: Specify identifiability assumptions and flag observationally indistinguishable signaling and environmental explanations.
On synthetic confounded tissues, achieve ≥80% precision at 50% recall for identifiable directed signaling edges.

nodes.content: Develop SignalSep: a masked ligand–receptor spatial model with latent environmental factors and observational-equivalence checks that abstain on unidentifiable directed edges.
When can a neighbor’s partially observed ligand profile distinguish directed signaling from an unmeasured niche factor affecting both cells?
Niche-independent sender-ligand variation predicts receptor-linked neighbor responses; when ligand and niche fields coincide, their effects are observationally indistinguishable.
Simulate NicheMix-1 tissues with 40% dropout and ligand–niche correlations 0.2 versus 1.0; assess SignalSep edge recovery and abstention.
On NicheMix-1, SignalSep reached 84% precision at 50% recall (r=0.2) and abstained on 96% of indistinguishable edges (r=1.0).
Adopt SignalSep with abstention: 84% precision at 50% recall clears the target, while 96% of indistinguishable edges are flagged.
Document SignalSep’s niche-independent ligand variation and receptor-specificity assumptions; validate ambiguity flags and ≥80% precision at 50% recall on NicheMix-2.
Simulate NicheMix-2 with 40% dropout, receptor-negative controls, and ligand–niche collinearity; audit SignalSep assumptions, edge precision, and abstention.
NicheMix-2 audit report records identifiability assumptions, precision at 50% recall, receptor-negative false positives, and collinearity-driven abstentions.
Independently verify the NicheMix-2 audit report against simulation ground truth, checking precision at 50% recall and collinear-edge abstention.
NicheMix-2 verification found 82% precision at 50% identifiable-edge recall, 3% receptor-negative false positives, and 93% collinear-edge abstention.
Can expression-dependent ligand dropout mimic niche-independent variation and produce falsely identifiable directed edges in SignalSep?
Simulate NicheMix-MNAR with ligand- and niche-dependent detection plus environmental-only controls; measure SignalSep false-edge calls and abstention.
On NicheMix-MNAR, SignalSep achieved 81% precision at 50% identifiable-edge recall and abstained on 91% of environmental-only candidates.
Reweight NicheMix-MNAR cells by estimated detection propensity, then test whether SignalSep’s receptor-linked edges persist against matched environmental-only controls.
After propensity reweighting, NicheMix-MNAR precision fell from 81% to 71% at 50% recall; matched controls exposed detection-driven edges.
Under which ligand–niche-dependent dropout regimes do SignalSep’s observational-equivalence checks flag apparent directed edges as ambiguous?
With ≥2-fold niche-dependent ligand detection, SignalSep underflags environmental mimics despite reweighting, while matched negative controls reveal ambiguity.
Calibrate a ≥2-fold niche-detection sweep against NicheMix-2 truth and MNAR baseline; seed reweighting-exposed false edges and compare ambiguity sensitivity.
At 2–4-fold niche-dependent detection, reweighted SignalSep flagged 43% of environmental mimics; matched controls raised ambiguity detection to 88%.
Test held-out NicheMix-MNAR tissues at 1.5-, 2-, and 3-fold detection bias; compare reweighted ambiguity flags with matched-control flags.
On held-out NicheMix-MNAR at 3-fold bias, reweighted SignalSep flagged 91% of environmental mimics versus matched controls’ 87%.
When do reciprocal ligand–receptor interactions make edge direction unidentifiable from cross-sectional spatial transcriptomics?
Calibrate dropout to the observed 43% and 91% mimic-flag rates; simulate reciprocal feedback and reversed-edge twins to test directional abstention.
In ReciprocalMix, SignalSep abstained on 89% of distribution-matched reversed-edge twins; identifiable asymmetric-feedback edges reached 83% precision at 50% recall.
Retain asymmetric-feedback directional calls, but flag reversed-edge twins as unresolved: ReciprocalMix achieved 83% precision at 50% recall and 89% abstention.
Formalize reversed-edge equivalence criteria, then benchmark abstention across reciprocal-feedback strengths and dropout regimes while retaining identifiable asymmetric calls.
Generate ReciprocalMix-Grid with feedback ratios 1:1–4:1 and 20–60% dropout; compare reversed-edge likelihoods, abstention, and directional precision.
ReciprocalMix-Grid benchmark package contains simulated tissues, reversed-edge likelihood comparisons, equivalence labels, and dropout-stratified abstention and precision tables.
Develop NicheMatch: compare receptor-positive and receptor-negative receivers around niche-matched senders, using missingness bounds to flag nonidentifiable directions.
Can receptor-negative receivers adequately control for niche effects when ligand and receptor dropout depend on local cell density?
Density-matched, independently verified receptor-negative controls suppress niche-only edges; transcript-zero controls misclassify receptor dropout and inflate false positives.
On DensityMix, compare verified and transcript-zero receptor-negative controls under density-dependent dropout; measure niche-only false positives and precision at 50% recall.
DensityMix: verified controls achieved 82% precision at 50% recall and 4% niche-only false positives; transcript-zero controls achieved 68% and 19%.
Benchmark NicheMatch on held-out DensityMix-2 using verified receptor-negative controls; evaluate precision at 50% recall and missingness-bound abstention.
On held-out DensityMix-2, NicheMatch reached 73% precision at 50% recall; missingness bounds flagged only 54% of niche-equivalent edges.
Develop PerturbMap: infer directed edges from mosaic ligand knockouts, paired receptor responses, and niche controls; abstain under perturbation spillover.
Simulate randomized mosaic knockouts with niche confounding, dropout, and spillover; document no-spillover assumptions and benchmark ≥80% precision at 50% recall.
Generate KO-Mosaic tissues with randomized sender ligand knockouts, 40% transcript dropout, and graded paracrine spillover; score PerturbMap against known edges.
KO-Mosaic benchmark contains randomized knockout maps, dropout masks, graded spillover labels, ground-truth directed edges, and PerturbMap scoring scripts.
Audit KO-Mosaic knockout randomization, dropout masks, and spillover labels; independently compute PerturbMap precision at 50% recall by spillover.
KO-Mosaic audit confirmed knockout randomization; PerturbMap achieved 87% precision at 50% recall without spillover and flagged 92% of high-spillover edges.
Can knockout-induced niche remodeling violate PerturbMap’s exclusion assumption even when sender knockouts are randomized?
Extend KO-Mosaic with knockout-driven hypoxia affecting receptor-negative receivers; measure PerturbMap false edges and abstention under randomized knockouts.
With knockout-driven hypoxia, PerturbMap precision dropped to 64% at 50% recall; 71% of niche-mediated false edges escaped abstention.
Which independently measured hypoxia markers allow PerturbMap to distinguish knockout-induced niche remodeling from receptor-specific signaling?
Retest PerturbMap on baseline and hypoxia KO-Mosaic using independent pimonidazole staining and oxygen-optode maps; compare precision and abstention.
On hypoxic KO-Mosaic, combined pimonidazole–optode adjustment restored 82% precision at 50% recall and flagged 86% of niche-mediated edges.
Require both independent hypoxia assays for PerturbMap calls; otherwise abstain, since combined adjustment restored 82% precision at 50% recall.
Validate pimonidazole–optode adjustment on held-out KO-Mosaic; audit assay coverage, exclusion violations, and ≥80% precision at 50% recall.
Run PerturbMap on held-out KO-Mosaic-2 with paired hypoxia assays; mask one assay per replicate and compare edge precision and abstention.
KO-Mosaic-2 validation report includes paired-assay coverage, assay-masking ablations, directed-edge precision, and exclusion-violation abstention by replicate.
Develop CrossNiche: infer sender-to-receiver edges from niche-invariant ligand–receptor responses, using environmental sentinels and missingness bounds to flag ambiguities.
Can unmeasured environmental factors shared across niches mimic invariant ligand–receptor responses despite environmental sentinels?
CrossNiche misclassifies invariant shared-factor effects when sentinels omit the factor, but abstains when sentinels track it.
Simulate CrossNiche-Null with invariant hypoxia across four niches; compare environmental-only edge calls using hypoxia-tracking versus unrelated sentinels.
On CrossNiche-Null, CrossNiche abstained on 90% of environmental-only edges with unrelated sentinels versus 92% with hypoxia-tracking sentinels.
Simulate CrossNiche-Shift with a hidden factor coupled to ligands across niches; vary sentinel correlation and measure environmental false calls.
On CrossNiche-Shift, unrelated sentinels mislabeled 27% of environmental edges as signaling; factor-tracking sentinels abstained on 91%.
When do coordinated sender–receiver composition shifts across niches make CrossNiche’s invariant responses indistinguishable from signaling?
Extend CrossNiche-Null and CrossNiche-Shift with coordinated sender–receiver abundance gradients; compare signaling false calls and abstention across sentinel types.
With coordinated composition gradients, unrelated sentinels yielded 32% environmental false calls; factor-tracking sentinels reduced them to 7%.
Require factor-tracking sentinels and composition adjustment for CrossNiche calls; unrelated sentinels produced 32% environmental false calls.
Benchmark composition-adjusted CrossNiche on held-out gradient tissues with factor-tracking sentinels; quantify indistinguishable-edge abstention and precision at 50% recall.
Generate held-out CrossNiche-Gradient tissues with 40% dropout and coupled abundance shifts; test adjusted edge rankings against equivalence labels.
CrossNiche-Gradient benchmark includes held-out tissues, factor-tracking sentinel maps, composition-adjusted rankings, equivalence labels, and abstention metrics.
Develop PulseTrace: infer direction from time-resolved spatial ligand pulses and receptor-specific response delays, flagging niche-synchronized alternatives under dropout.
Simulate eight-frame spatial pulse series with 40% dropout; test temporal resolution assumptions, niche-synchronized abstention, and ≥80% precision at 50% recall.
Construct eight-frame PulseTrace simulations using ReciprocalMix-Grid equivalence labels, KO-Mosaic-2 assay-coverage patterns, and CrossNiche-Gradient sentinel maps; score 40%-dropout edge recovery.
PulseTrace-8 benchmark contains eight-frame tissues, 40% dropout masks, niche-synchronized controls, equivalence labels, and precision-at-50%-recall scoring code.
Audit PulseTrace-8 timing and equivalence labels; independently score directional precision at 50% recall and niche-synchronized abstention.
PulseTrace-8 audit found 85% directional precision at 50% identifiable-edge recall and 90% abstention on niche-synchronized controls.
Can asynchronous niche fluctuations generate ligand-leading response delays that PulseTrace mistakes for directed signaling?
Niche waves lagging across cell types by one frame create false ligand-leading edges unless independent niche sensors capture propagation.
Using PulseTrace-8 baseline and DensityMix-2 missed niche-equivalent cases, simulate one-frame niche waves; compare false-call rates with versus without independent sensors.
On one-frame niche waves, PulseTrace falsely called 4% of environmental edges without sensors versus 3% with sensors.
Retain PulseTrace without mandatory niche sensors: one-frame waves yielded 4% environmental false calls; precision reached 85% at 50% recall.
Revise eight-frame validation: make niche sensors optional; test irregular multi-frame waves at 40% dropout, tracking precision and abstention.
Extend PulseTrace-8 with irregular 2–3-frame niche waves at 40% dropout; compare precision and environmental-edge abstention with versus without sensors.
PulseTrace-8 v2 adds irregular 2–3-frame niche waves, optional-sensor ablations, and dropout-stratified precision and abstention tables.
